messages.content: What is Re-frame and how does its architecture work?

Re-frame is a ClojureScript framework for building SPAs using a unidirectional data flow pattern. It's built on top of Reagent.

**The 6 Dominoes Architecture**
```
1. Event Dispatch    → User clicks button
2. Event Handling    → Handler processes event, produces effects
3. Effect Handling   → Effects are executed (DB change, HTTP, etc.)
4. Query (Sub)       → Subscription extracts data from app-db
5. View              → Reagent component renders UI
6. DOM               → Browser updates screen
```

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {re-frame/re-frame {:mvn/version "1.3.0"}
        reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "1.2.0"}}}

;; Namespace
(ns myapp.core
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
```

**The App Database (app-db)**
```clojure
;; All application state lives in a single atom
;; Re-frame manages this for you - you never touch it directly

;; Initialize app-db with an event
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::initialize-db
  (fn [_ _]
    {:user nil
     :items []
     :loading? false
     :current-page :home}))

;; Dispatch at app start
(rf/dispatch-sync [::initialize-db])
```

**Events - Domino 1 & 2**
```clojure
;; Events are vectors: [event-id & args]
(rf/dispatch [:add-item {:name "New Item"}])
(rf/dispatch [:set-page :about])
(rf/dispatch [:fetch-user 123])
```

**Subscriptions - Domino 4**
```clojure
;; Subscribe to app-db data
(rf/reg-sub
  ::items
  (fn [db _]
    (:items db)))

;; Use in components
(defn items-list []
  (let [items @(rf/subscribe [::items])]
    [:ul
      (for [item items]
        ^{:key (:id item)}
        [:li (:name item)])]))
```

**Views - Domino 5**
```clojure
;; Reagent components that:
;; 1. Subscribe to data
;; 2. Dispatch events

(defn counter []
  (let [count @(rf/subscribe [::count])]
    [:div
      [:p "Count: " count]
      [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [::increment])} "+"]
      [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [::decrement])} "-"]]))
```

**Complete Flow Example**
```clojure
(ns myapp.core
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [reagent.dom :as rdom]))

;; -- Events --
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::init
  (fn [_ _]
    {:count 0}))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::increment
  (fn [db _]
    (update db :count inc)))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::decrement
  (fn [db _]
    (update db :count dec)))

;; -- Subscriptions --
(rf/reg-sub
  ::count
  (fn [db _]
    (:count db)))

;; -- Views --
(defn counter []
  (let [count @(rf/subscribe [::count])]
    [:div.counter
      [:h1 "Count: " count]
      [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [::increment])} "Increment"]
      [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [::decrement])} "Decrement"]]))

(defn app []
  [:div
    [:h1 "Re-frame Counter"]
    [counter]])

;; -- Entry Point --
(defn ^:export init []
  (rf/dispatch-sync [::init])
  (rdom/render [app] (.getElementById js/document "app")))
```
How do I register and use events in Re-frame?

Re-frame has two types of event handlers: `reg-event-db` for pure database updates and `reg-event-fx` for effects.

**reg-event-db - Pure DB Updates**
```clojure
;; Handler receives: [db event-vector]
;; Returns: new db

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::set-user
  (fn [db [_ user]]         ; Destructure event vector
    (assoc db :user user)))  ; Return new db

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::add-item
  (fn [db [_ item]]
    (update db :items conj item)))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::remove-item
  (fn [db [_ item-id]]
    (update db :items (fn [items]
                        (remove #(= (:id %) item-id) items)))))

;; Dispatching
(rf/dispatch [::set-user {:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}])
(rf/dispatch [::add-item {:id 1 :name "New Item"}])
(rf/dispatch [::remove-item 1])
```

**reg-event-fx - Side Effects**
```clojure
;; Handler receives: [coeffects event-vector]
;; Returns: map of effects to execute

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::fetch-users
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    {:db (assoc db :loading? true)
     :http-xhrio {:method :get
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :on-success [::users-loaded]
                  :on-failure [::api-error]}}))

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::users-loaded
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ users]]
    {:db (-> db
             (assoc :users users)
             (assoc :loading? false))}))

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::save-and-notify
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ data]]
    {:db (assoc db :data data)
     :dispatch [::show-notification "Saved!"]
     :local-storage {:key "data" :value data}}))
```

**Built-in Effects**
```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::complex-operation
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ data]]
    {;; Update database
     :db (assoc db :data data)
     
     ;; Dispatch another event
     :dispatch [::other-event data]
     
     ;; Dispatch multiple events
     :dispatch-n [[::event-1] [::event-2 data]]
     
     ;; Dispatch after delay (ms)
     :dispatch-later [{:ms 1000 :dispatch [::delayed-event]}]
     
     ;; For debugging
     :fx [[:dispatch [::event-a]]
          [:dispatch [::event-b]]]}))
```

**Interceptors**
```clojure
;; Interceptors are middleware for events

;; Built-in: path - focus on part of db
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::update-user-name
  [(rf/path :user)]  ; Only receives/returns (:user db)
  (fn [user [_ name]]
    (assoc user :name name)))

;; Built-in: debug - logs events
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::my-event
  [rf/debug]  ; Logs before/after db
  (fn [db [_ data]]
    (assoc db :data data)))

;; Built-in: trim-v - removes event id from vector
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::set-value
  [rf/trim-v]
  (fn [db [value]]  ; No need to skip event-id
    (assoc db :value value)))

;; Combine interceptors
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::update-setting
  [rf/debug (rf/path :settings) rf/trim-v]
  (fn [settings [key value]]
    (assoc settings key value)))
```

**Custom Interceptors**
```clojure
(def validate-user
  (rf/->interceptor
    :id :validate-user
    :before (fn [context]
              (let [event (get-in context [:coeffects :event])
                    user (second event)]
                (if (valid-user? user)
                  context  ; Continue
                  (assoc context :queue []))))  ; Stop processing
    :after (fn [context]
             context)))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::create-user
  [validate-user]
  (fn [db [_ user]]
    (update db :users conj user)))
```

**Event Helpers**
```clojure
;; dispatch-sync - synchronous, blocks
(rf/dispatch-sync [::init])  ; Use for initialization

;; dispatch - asynchronous (normal use)
(rf/dispatch [::my-event data])

;; Check if event is registered
(rf/clear-event :my-event)  ; Remove handler
```
How do I create and use subscriptions in Re-frame?

Subscriptions extract and compute data from app-db for views. They're cached and only recompute when dependencies change.

**Basic Subscriptions**
```clojure
;; Simple extraction
(rf/reg-sub
  ::user
  (fn [db _]
    (:user db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::items
  (fn [db _]
    (:items db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::loading?
  (fn [db _]
    (:loading? db)))

;; Usage in components
(defn user-greeting []
  (let [user @(rf/subscribe [::user])]
    [:div "Hello, " (:name user)]))
```

**Subscriptions with Parameters**
```clojure
(rf/reg-sub
  ::item-by-id
  (fn [db [_ item-id]]   ; Destructure the subscription vector
    (first (filter #(= (:id %) item-id) (:items db)))))

;; Usage
(let [item @(rf/subscribe [::item-by-id 123])]
  [:div (:name item)])
```

**Derived/Computed Subscriptions (Layer 2)**
```clojure
;; Layer 2 subs depend on other subs, not directly on db

;; Base subscriptions (Layer 2)
(rf/reg-sub
  ::items
  (fn [db _]
    (:items db)))

;; Derived subscription (Layer 3)
(rf/reg-sub
  ::active-items
  :<- [::items]  ; Depends on ::items subscription
  (fn [items _]
    (filter :active? items)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::item-count
  :<- [::items]
  (fn [items _]
    (count items)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::active-count
  :<- [::active-items]
  (fn [active-items _]
    (count active-items)))
```

**Multiple Dependencies**
```clojure
(rf/reg-sub
  ::filtered-sorted-items
  :<- [::items]
  :<- [::filter-text]
  :<- [::sort-key]
  (fn [[items filter-text sort-key] _]
    (->> items
         (filter #(clojure.string/includes? 
                    (clojure.string/lower-case (:name %))
                    (clojure.string/lower-case filter-text)))
         (sort-by sort-key))))

;; Using a function for dynamic dependencies
(rf/reg-sub
  ::user-items
  (fn [[_ user-id]]  ; Query vector
    [(rf/subscribe [::items])
     (rf/subscribe [::user-by-id user-id])])
  (fn [[items user] [_ user-id]]
    (filter #(= (:owner-id %) user-id) items)))
```

**Subscription Patterns**
```clojure
;; Pattern: Selector subscriptions
(rf/reg-sub ::db (fn [db _] db))  ; Raw db access (use sparingly)

(rf/reg-sub
  ::user-name
  :<- [::user]
  (fn [user _]
    (:name user)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::user-email
  :<- [::user]
  (fn [user _]
    (:email user)))

;; Pattern: Materialized views
(rf/reg-sub
  ::items-by-category
  :<- [::items]
  (fn [items _]
    (group-by :category items)))

;; Pattern: Aggregations
(rf/reg-sub
  ::total-price
  :<- [::cart-items]
  (fn [items _]
    (reduce + 0 (map :price items))))
```

**Using Subscriptions Efficiently**
```clojure
;; BAD: Subscribe in parent, pass data down
(defn parent []
  (let [items @(rf/subscribe [::items])]
    [:div
      (for [item items]
        ^{:key (:id item)}
        [item-component item])]))

;; BETTER: Each component subscribes to what it needs
(defn item-component [item-id]
  (let [item @(rf/subscribe [::item-by-id item-id])]
    [:div (:name item)]))

(defn parent []
  (let [item-ids @(rf/subscribe [::item-ids])]
    [:div
      (for [id item-ids]
        ^{:key id}
        [item-component id])]))
```

**Subscription Best Practices**
```clojure
;; 1. Keep subscriptions small and focused
(rf/reg-sub ::user-name :<- [::user] (fn [u _] (:name u)))
(rf/reg-sub ::user-email :<- [::user] (fn [u _] (:email u)))

;; 2. Use descriptive names
(rf/reg-sub ::active-users-sorted-by-name ...)

;; 3. Document complex subscriptions
(rf/reg-sub
  ::dashboard-data
  ;; "Aggregates user stats, recent activity, and notifications
  ;;  for the dashboard view. Updates when any dependency changes."
  :<- [::user-stats]
  :<- [::recent-activity]
  :<- [::unread-notifications]
  (fn [[stats activity notifications] _]
    {:stats stats
     :activity (take 5 activity)
     :notification-count (count notifications)}))

;; 4. Use re-frame-10x for debugging subscriptions
;; It shows subscription graph and values
```
How do I handle HTTP requests and other side effects in Re-frame?

Re-frame handles side effects through the effects system. The most common library for HTTP is `re-frame-http-fx`.

**Setup HTTP Effects**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {day8.re-frame/http-fx {:mvn/version "0.2.4"}}}

;; Require in your namespace
(ns myapp.events
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [day8.re-frame.http-fx]  ; Just require, registers :http-xhrio effect
            [ajax.core :as ajax]))
```

**Basic HTTP Request**
```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::fetch-users
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    {:db (assoc db :loading? true)
     :http-xhrio {:method :get
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :response-format (ajax/json-response-format {:keywords? true})
                  :on-success [::fetch-users-success]
                  :on-failure [::api-error]}}))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::fetch-users-success
  (fn [db [_ response]]
    (-> db
        (assoc :users response)
        (assoc :loading? false))))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::api-error
  (fn [db [_ error]]
    (-> db
        (assoc :error (:status-text error))
        (assoc :loading? false))))
```

**POST Request with Body**
```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::create-user
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ user-data]]
    {:db (assoc db :saving? true)
     :http-xhrio {:method :post
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :params user-data
                  :format (ajax/json-request-format)
                  :response-format (ajax/json-response-format {:keywords? true})
                  :on-success [::create-user-success]
                  :on-failure [::api-error]}}))

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::create-user-success
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ new-user]]
    {:db (-> db
             (update :users conj new-user)
             (assoc :saving? false))
     :dispatch [::show-notification "User created!"]}))
```

**Custom Effect Handlers**
```clojure
;; Register a custom effect
(rf/reg-fx
  :local-storage
  (fn [{:keys [key value]}]
    (.setItem js/localStorage key (js/JSON.stringify (clj->js value)))))

(rf/reg-fx
  :navigate
  (fn [route]
    ;; Use your routing library here
    (set! (.-href js/location) route)))

(rf/reg-fx
  :console-log
  (fn [message]
    (js/console.log message)))

;; Using custom effects
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::save-settings
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ settings]]
    {:db (assoc db :settings settings)
     :local-storage {:key "settings" :value settings}
     :dispatch [::show-notification "Settings saved!"]}))
```

**Coeffects - Injecting External Data**
```clojure
;; Register a coeffect handler
(rf/reg-cofx
  :now
  (fn [cofx _]
    (assoc cofx :now (js/Date.))))

(rf/reg-cofx
  :local-storage
  (fn [cofx key]
    (assoc cofx :local-storage 
           (js->clj (js/JSON.parse (.getItem js/localStorage key))
                    :keywordize-keys true))))

;; Inject coeffects into event
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::initialize
  [(rf/inject-cofx :local-storage "settings")
   (rf/inject-cofx :now)]
  (fn [{:keys [db local-storage now]} _]
    {:db (-> db
             (assoc :settings (or local-storage {}))
             (assoc :initialized-at now))}))
```

**Debouncing Effects**
```clojure
;; Using dispatch-debounce effect (from re-frame-debounce-fx)
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::search-input-changed
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ search-term]]
    {:db (assoc db :search-term search-term)
     :dispatch-debounce {:id ::search
                         :timeout 300
                         :dispatch [::do-search search-term]}}))

;; Or implement simple debounce yourself
(defonce search-timeout (atom nil))

(rf/reg-fx
  :search-debounce
  (fn [{:keys [timeout dispatch]}]
    (when @search-timeout
      (js/clearTimeout @search-timeout))
    (reset! search-timeout
      (js/setTimeout #(rf/dispatch dispatch) timeout))))
```

**Async/Await Pattern with core.async**
```clojure
(require '[cljs.core.async :refer [go <!]])

(rf/reg-fx
  :async-operation
  (fn [{:keys [operation on-success on-failure]}]
    (go
      (try
        (let [result (<! (operation))]
          (rf/dispatch (conj on-success result)))
        (catch js/Error e
          (rf/dispatch (conj on-failure e)))))))
```

**Error Handling Pattern**
```clojure
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::api-error
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ {:keys [status status-text response]}]]
    (let [error-message (case status
                          401 "Please log in"
                          403 "You don't have permission"
                          404 "Not found"
                          500 "Server error, please try again"
                          (or (:message response) status-text "Unknown error"))]
      {:db (-> db
               (assoc :loading? false)
               (assoc :error error-message))
       :dispatch (when (= status 401)
                   [::redirect-to-login])})))
```
Show me how to structure a complete Re-frame application.

Here's a well-structured Re-frame application with clear separation of concerns:

**Project Structure**
```
src/
└── myapp/
    ├── core.cljs          ; Entry point
    ├── db.cljs            ; Initial state and spec
    ├── events.cljs        ; Event handlers
    ├── subs.cljs          ; Subscriptions
    ├── views.cljs         ; UI components
    ├── routes.cljs        ; Routing
    └── config.cljs        ; Configuration
```

**db.cljs - Database Schema**
```clojure
(ns myapp.db
  (:require [cljs.spec.alpha :as s]))

;; Spec for app-db (optional but recommended)
(s/def ::id int?)
(s/def ::name string?)
(s/def ::email string?)
(s/def ::user (s/keys :req-un [::id ::name ::email]))
(s/def ::users (s/coll-of ::user))
(s/def ::loading? boolean?)
(s/def ::error (s/nilable string?))
(s/def ::current-page keyword?)

(s/def ::db
  (s/keys :req-un [::users ::loading? ::error ::current-page]
          :opt-un [::user]))

;; Initial database value
(def default-db
  {:users []
   :user nil
   :loading? false
   :error nil
   :current-page :home})
```

**events.cljs - Event Handlers**
```clojure
(ns myapp.events
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [myapp.db :as db]
            [day8.re-frame.http-fx]
            [ajax.core :as ajax]))

;; -- Initialization --
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::initialize-db
  (fn [_ _]
    db/default-db))

;; -- Navigation --
(rf/reg-event-db
  ::set-active-page
  (fn [db [_ page]]
    (assoc db :current-page page)))

;; -- User Events --
(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::fetch-users
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    {:db (assoc db :loading? true :error nil)
     :http-xhrio {:method :get
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :response-format (ajax/json-response-format {:keywords? true})
                  :on-success [::fetch-users-success]
                  :on-failure [::api-failure]}}))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::fetch-users-success
  (fn [db [_ users]]
    (-> db
        (assoc :users users)
        (assoc :loading? false))))

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::create-user
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ user-data]]
    {:db (assoc db :loading? true)
     :http-xhrio {:method :post
                  :uri "/api/users"
                  :params user-data
                  :format (ajax/json-request-format)
                  :response-format (ajax/json-response-format {:keywords? true})
                  :on-success [::create-user-success]
                  :on-failure [::api-failure]}}))

(rf/reg-event-fx
  ::create-user-success
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ user]]
    {:db (-> db
             (update :users conj user)
             (assoc :loading? false))
     :dispatch [::set-active-page :users]}))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::api-failure
  (fn [db [_ {:keys [status status-text]}]]
    (-> db
        (assoc :error (str "Error " status ": " status-text))
        (assoc :loading? false))))

(rf/reg-event-db
  ::clear-error
  (fn [db _]
    (assoc db :error nil)))
```

**subs.cljs - Subscriptions**
```clojure
(ns myapp.subs
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]))

;; -- Layer 2: Direct DB access --
(rf/reg-sub
  ::users
  (fn [db _]
    (:users db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::current-user
  (fn [db _]
    (:user db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::loading?
  (fn [db _]
    (:loading? db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::error
  (fn [db _]
    (:error db)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::current-page
  (fn [db _]
    (:current-page db)))

;; -- Layer 3: Derived subscriptions --
(rf/reg-sub
  ::user-count
  :<- [::users]
  (fn [users _]
    (count users)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::sorted-users
  :<- [::users]
  (fn [users _]
    (sort-by :name users)))

(rf/reg-sub
  ::user-by-id
  :<- [::users]
  (fn [users [_ user-id]]
    (first (filter #(= (:id %) user-id) users))))
```

**views.cljs - UI Components**
```clojure
(ns myapp.views
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [myapp.subs :as subs]
            [myapp.events :as events]))

;; -- Layout Components --
(defn navbar []
  (let [current-page @(rf/subscribe [::subs/current-page])]
    [:nav.navbar
      [:a {:class (when (= current-page :home) "active")
           :on-click #(rf/dispatch [::events/set-active-page :home])}
        "Home"]
      [:a {:class (when (= current-page :users) "active")
           :on-click #(rf/dispatch [::events/set-active-page :users])}
        "Users"]]))

(defn error-banner []
  (let [error @(rf/subscribe [::subs/error])]
    (when error
      [:div.error-banner
        [:span error]
        [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [::events/clear-error])} "×"]])))

(defn loading-spinner []
  [:div.loading-spinner "Loading..."])

;; -- Page Components --
(defn home-page []
  [:div.page.home
    [:h1 "Welcome to MyApp"]
    [:p "This is a Re-frame application."]])

(defn user-card [user]
  [:div.user-card {:key (:id user)}
    [:h3 (:name user)]
    [:p (:email user)]])

(defn user-form []
  (let [form-data (reagent.core/atom {:name "" :email ""})]
    (fn []
      [:form.user-form {:on-submit (fn [e]
                                     (.preventDefault e)
                                     (rf/dispatch [::events/create-user @form-data])
                                     (reset! form-data {:name "" :email ""}))}
        [:input {:placeholder "Name"
                 :value (:name @form-data)
                 :on-change #(swap! form-data assoc :name (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:input {:placeholder "Email"
                 :value (:email @form-data)
                 :on-change #(swap! form-data assoc :email (.. % -target -value))}]
        [:button {:type "submit"} "Add User"]])))

(defn users-page []
  (let [users @(rf/subscribe [::subs/sorted-users])
        loading? @(rf/subscribe [::subs/loading?])]
    [:div.page.users
      [:h1 "Users"]
      [user-form]
      (if loading?
        [loading-spinner]
        [:div.users-list
          (for [user users]
            ^{:key (:id user)}
            [user-card user])])]))

;; -- Main App --
(defn main-panel []
  (let [current-page @(rf/subscribe [::subs/current-page])]
    [:div.app
      [navbar]
      [error-banner]
      (case current-page
        :home [home-page]
        :users [users-page]
        [:div "Page not found"])]))
```

**core.cljs - Entry Point**
```clojure
(ns myapp.core
  (:require [reagent.dom :as rdom]
            [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [myapp.events :as events]
            [myapp.views :as views]
            [myapp.subs]))

(defn dev-setup []
  (when ^boolean goog.DEBUG
    (enable-console-print!)
    (println "dev mode")))

(defn ^:dev/after-load mount-root []
  (rf/clear-subscription-cache!)
  (let [root-el (.getElementById js/document "app")]
    (rdom/unmount-component-at-node root-el)
    (rdom/render [views/main-panel] root-el)))

(defn ^:export init []
  (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
  (dev-setup)
  (mount-root)
  ;; Fetch initial data
  (rf/dispatch [::events/fetch-users]))
```
How do I test Re-frame events and subscriptions?

Re-frame provides excellent testing support. You can test events, subscriptions, and views in isolation.

**Testing Event Handlers**
```clojure
(ns myapp.events-test
  (:require [cljs.test :refer-macros [deftest is testing]]
            [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [day8.re-frame.test :as rf-test]
            [myapp.events :as events]
            [myapp.subs :as subs]))

;; Test reg-event-db handlers directly
(deftest test-set-user
  (testing "set-user event updates db correctly"
    (let [db {:user nil :loading? false}
          new-user {:id 1 :name "Alice"}
          ;; Get the handler function
          handler (-> (rf/get-handler :event :myapp.events/set-user)
                      :handler)]
      ;; Call handler directly
      (is (= {:user new-user :loading? false}
             (handler db [::events/set-user new-user]))))))

;; Or test with run-test-sync
(deftest test-event-updates-db
  (rf-test/run-test-sync
    ;; Setup
    (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
    
    ;; Action
    (rf/dispatch [::events/set-active-page :users])
    
    ;; Assert
    (is (= :users @(rf/subscribe [::subs/current-page])))))
```

**Testing with Effects**
```clojure
(deftest test-fetch-users-event
  (rf-test/run-test-sync
    ;; Initialize
    (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
    
    ;; Replace :http-xhrio effect with mock
    (rf/reg-fx :http-xhrio
      (fn [request]
        ;; Simulate success
        (rf/dispatch (:on-success request)
                     [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}
                      {:id 2 :name "Bob"}])))
    
    ;; Dispatch event that triggers HTTP
    (rf/dispatch [::events/fetch-users])
    
    ;; Check results
    (is (= 2 (count @(rf/subscribe [::subs/users]))))
    (is (= false @(rf/subscribe [::subs/loading?])))))

;; Test that correct effects are produced
(deftest test-fetch-users-produces-correct-effects
  (let [coeffects {:db {:loading? false :users []}}
        event [::events/fetch-users]
        ;; Get the handler
        handler (-> (rf/get-handler :event ::events/fetch-users)
                    :handler)
        ;; Run handler
        effects (handler coeffects event)]
    
    ;; Check db effect
    (is (= true (get-in effects [:db :loading?])))
    
    ;; Check http effect was requested
    (is (some? (:http-xhrio effects)))
    (is (= :get (get-in effects [:http-xhrio :method])))
    (is (= "/api/users" (get-in effects [:http-xhrio :uri])))))
```

**Testing Subscriptions**
```clojure
(deftest test-subscriptions
  (rf-test/run-test-sync
    ;; Setup test db
    (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
    
    ;; Manually update db for testing
    (reset! re-frame.db/app-db
            {:users [{:id 1 :name "Bob"}
                     {:id 2 :name "Alice"}]
             :loading? false
             :current-page :home})
    
    ;; Test subscriptions
    (testing "::users returns all users"
      (is (= 2 (count @(rf/subscribe [::subs/users])))))
    
    (testing "::sorted-users returns users sorted by name"
      (let [sorted @(rf/subscribe [::subs/sorted-users])]
        (is (= "Alice" (:name (first sorted))))
        (is (= "Bob" (:name (second sorted))))))
    
    (testing "::user-by-id finds correct user"
      (let [user @(rf/subscribe [::subs/user-by-id 1])]
        (is (= "Bob" (:name user)))))))
```

**Testing Async Operations**
```clojure
(deftest test-async-flow
  (rf-test/run-test-async
    ;; Initialize
    (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
    
    ;; Mock HTTP
    (rf/reg-fx :http-xhrio
      (fn [{:keys [on-success]}]
        ;; Simulate async delay
        (js/setTimeout
          #(rf/dispatch (conj on-success [{:id 1 :name "Test"}]))
          100)))
    
    ;; Dispatch
    (rf/dispatch [::events/fetch-users])
    
    ;; Wait for async completion
    (rf-test/wait-for [::events/fetch-users-success]
      (is (= 1 (count @(rf/subscribe [::subs/users])))))))
```

```clojure
(ns myapp.views-test
  (:require [cljs.test :refer-macros [deftest is testing]]

;; Test that view subscribes to correct data
(deftest test-user-card-renders

    (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
    
    (let [component (views/user-card {:id 1 :name "Alice" :email "a@b.com"})

      ;; Check component structure
      (is (= :div.user-card (first component)))
      (is (some #(= "Alice" %) (flatten component))))))

;; Integration test with mock subscriptions
(deftest test-users-page-shows-loading
  (rf-test/run-test-sync
    ;; Setup with loading state
    (reset! re-frame.db/app-db {:users [] :loading? true})
    
    ;; Render component
    (let [component (views/users-page)]
      ;; Check for loading indicator
      (is (some #{[views/loading-spinner]} (tree-seq vector? seq component))))))
```

**Test Fixtures**
```clojure
(defn test-fixtures []
  ;; Reset db before each test
  (rf/dispatch-sync [::events/initialize-db])
  ;; Clear subscription cache
  (rf/clear-subscription-cache!))

(cljs.test/use-fixtures :each {:before test-fixtures})

;; Reusable test helpers
(defn with-test-db [db-state test-fn]
  (rf-test/run-test-sync
    (reset! re-frame.db/app-db db-state)
    (test-fn)))

(deftest test-with-custom-db
  (with-test-db {:users [{:id 1 :name "Test"}] :loading? false}
    (fn []
      (is (= 1 @(rf/subscribe [::subs/user-count]))))))
```
